summary: Decision training data regenerated from neutral, grammatical templates (standard German spelling, nothing real), tf-idf router model retrained (skirnir-tfidf-v2, records data_sha256), router 0.25.1. New CI check test/check_training_data.py rebuilds both data sets, compares them with the committed files, checks spelling and the model's data digest; selftests cover the rejected cases. Privacy head training (decision-embed/privacy/train_privacy.py): embeddings one text at a time as the service computes them, threshold from out-of-fold scores over five template folds, head on all templates, default recall target 0.98, refuses too few templates, lowest threshold without evidence (ADR-0078, proposed). Traced B7: the router reads 'personal' and 'threshold' from POST /privacy (privacy.py), a configured router.cloud.privacy_check.threshold overrides the head's; the service (server.py, unchanged) loads the new privacy.json (same keys, extra result fields ignored) - verified on loopback: model skirnir-privacy-e5-small-v2, threshold 0.30. The tf-idf model keeps the keys load_model requires; the extra data_sha256 is ignored by the router. B9: two CI steps run repository stdlib scripts; no new dependency, action or secret. No router code path changed except VERSION; nothing was deployed.

findings.evidence: The privacy classifier has false negatives by design (B7). Over 20 template splits the earlier threshold procedure gave test recall 0.898 +/- 0.082 (worst 0.76) at target 0.98; the new one 0.964 +/- 0.012 (worst 0.96) at unchanged precision. The head written now (threshold 0.30) finds 50/50 personal test requests and flags 3/50 neutral ones; the head in use had 0.40, 50/50, 1/50.
findings.resolution: This change lowers the residual risk in expectation and makes the threshold stable; it does not remove it. Uncovered content (calendar entries, motion history) is documented as proposals. The rules layer and cloud:false remain the stronger controls. The retrained head reaches a router only when the operator deploys it.

findings.evidence: The CI workflow gains two steps (selftest/check training data, selftest privacy threshold).
findings.resolution: They run scripts from the repository with the standard library only, install nothing, use no secret and no new action; the builders they start are repository code. Flagged for maintainer review as a workflow change.

limitations: The embedding head and the privacy head are not in the repository and were not deployed; they were trained and measured locally on a CPU.
If router.cloud.privacy_check.threshold is set in a configuration, it overrides the new head's threshold; with the new head it should be null.
The privacy test set has 100 hand-written sentences and has now been looked at; a fresh one is proposed.
The end-to-end suite ran on Windows; CI runs the Python checks on Linux.
